old: Its root once meant simply looking after a home — animals included.
The French word behind it, ménager, means "to keep house."
Related to ménager, this word now names a collection of wild animals on display.
clues: This noun for a kind of collection began with housework: it comes from a French verb meaning "to keep house."
Because housekeeping once included tending domestic animals, it came to mean a collection of exotic animals kept for display, often grander or more private than a zoo.
Figuratively, it describes a lively, mixed assortment of odd characters, and Tennessee Williams named a famous play The Glass ___ after a collection of tiny animal figurines.
